entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0386: `AsyncFd::new` and related constructors violate I/O safety
entry.content:
`AsyncFd::new` and related constructors violate I/O safety

Affected:

  • tokio — fixed in 1.51.6, 1.53.3

`tokio::io::unix::AsyncFd` provides safe constructors (`new`, `with_interest`, `try_new`, and `try_with_interest`) that accept any `T: AsRawFd` rather than requiring proof of ownership or validity of the file descriptor. Because `RawFd` implements `AsRawFd`, safe code can construct an `AsyncFd` from an arbitrary or closed file descriptor, or close/replace the underlying file descriptor while the `AsyncFd` is still alive. This violates I/O safety in two ways: 1. `AsyncFd<T>` implements `AsFd` for all `T: AsRawFd` by calling `BorrowedFd::borrow_raw(self.as_raw_fd())`, allowing safe code to obtain an arbitrary `BorrowedFd<'_>` without owning the file descriptor. 2. Tokio's I/O driver stores a pointer to an internal allocation in the `epoll`/`kqueue` user data for registered file descriptors…

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0385: Non-constant-time mask generation and `u128` comparisons
entry.content:
Non-constant-time mask generation and `u128` comparisons

Affected:

  • ctutils — fixed in 0.4.4

## Summary The `ctutils::Choice` type has mask generation functions for each unsigned integer size (`u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`, `u128`). These are `const fn` and therefore can't reuse the `asm!`-backed mask generation in the `cmov` crate that's otherwise used to ensure constant-time. In releases prior to v0.4.4, the generated code from these functions could include a branch on commonly used platforms. This has been corrected in this release and now verified on several platforms using BINSEC. Additionally, `u128` comparison operations provided via `ctutils::Choice` and intended to work in constant-time were generating branches on 32-bit targets. This has been resolved via a special case implementation of these functions for such targets. ## Impact Branch instructions on secret values ca…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0305: Use-after-free when XML includes have duplicated entities
entry.content:
Use-after-free when XML includes have duplicated entities

Aliases: CVE-2026-96889, GHSA-cpvr-w4j5-2mpg

Affected:

  • librsvg — fixed in 2.57.5, 2.60.3, 2.61.5, 2.62.4, 2.63.2

Librsvg uses libxml2, a C library, to parse XML. When librsvg parses an SVG document which has a nested Xinclude, an XML entity declaration with a duplicate name as an existing one can cause a use-after-free error. While libxml2 is expanding an internal entity, a recursive XInclude can parse another document that declares an entity with the same name. Both parses use the same `XmlState` entity map on the librsvg side. `entity_insert()` replaces the first entry, whose `Drop` implementation calls `xmlFreeNode()`. The outer `xmlCtxtParseEntity()` then keeps using the freed 144-byte `xmlEntity`. The included parse should not free an entity that the outer parser is still using. The fix is in commit 8a1b0cd319e9af2d1e9cf878081dd77f227a0504, where librsvg will no longer free xmlEntity pointer…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-9jh8-v38h-cvhr: ammonia: mXSS via MathML `annotation-xml` encoding strip

Severity: CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N

  • ammonia — fixed in 4.1.3

If a certain set of MathML tags are enabled, an attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript code into the user's browser. The `annotation-xml` tag has slightly different behavior than the other "integration point" tags in MathML and SVG, but ammonia didn't handle it, so it didn't correctly strip the namespace-incompatible tags. This vulnerability only has an effect when the `math` and `annotation-xml` tags are both enabled, but the `encoding` attribute is disabled, because it relies on the following sequence of steps: 1. User writes code like `<math><annotation-xml encoding="text/html"><gadget></annotation-xml></math>`. 2. Namespace filtering checks the DOM, and it passes. `<gadget>` is parsed as HTML. 3. Attribute filter strips it down to `<math><annotation-xml><gadget></annotation-xml></…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0384: Race condition in `tokio::time::Interval` on Tokio v1.54.0
entry.content:
Race condition in `tokio::time::Interval` on Tokio v1.54.0

Aliases: GHSA-5wjr-9356-4wc8

Affected:

  • tokio — fixed in 1.54.1

## Summary On the multi-threaded runtime, there is a race condition between `Interval::poll_tick` and the runtime's time driver. This affects `Interval` only. `Sleep` and `Timeout` are **not** affected. ## Details In Tokio v1.54.0, a race condition between `tokio::time::Interval::poll_tick` (including `.tick().await`) and the runtime time driver can drop an internal timer entry without synchronizing with the driver thread that is firing it. This causes a data race and use-after-free on the timer's waker and task state in safe Rust, leading to assertion panics, task reference-count corruption, or heap memory corruption.
